anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
Case A: pending required check, watch window expired

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. The ticket's requirement that the health endpoint report the build version is covered, and the README describes that behavior correctly.

Nothing blocks merging except one required check, the unit tests (test_unit), which is still running on the commit being reviewed. The 15-minute watch ended before it finished, and nothing has failed.

I recommend deliver because another watch window can see the unit tests finish and then offer the merge.

Pick one:
1. deliver - watch the still-running unit tests for one more 15-minute window and continue until merge is offered; the repair and sync attempt limits stay as they are. [recommended]
2. assess - stop the delivery work and post nothing, since no problems are open.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case B: GitHub blocks the merge, with no override

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. The ticket's requirement that the health endpoint report the build version is covered, and the README describes that behavior correctly.

One thing blocks merging: GitHub requires an approving review from someone other than you, and your access has no admin override. Both required checks, the unit tests and the image build, passed. GitHub blocks this actor from merging, and no local repair applies.

I recommend stop because only another reviewer's approval can unblock this merge, and nothing this run can do supplies it.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - once another reviewer has approved, retry the merge check and continue the work, with 10 more repair and 10 more sync attempts allowed.
3. assess - stop the delivery work and post nothing, since no problems are open.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case C: held workflow run and no repair attempts left

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. The ticket's requirement that the health endpoint report the build version is covered, and the README describes that behavior correctly.

One thing blocks merging: the required unit-test check cannot start until a repository maintainer approves its workflow run. The repair attempts allowed for this run are also used up. This is the same missing approval that stopped the last attempt, and it has not changed. Approving the held workflow run needs maintainer permission, which you do not have.

I recommend stop because only a maintainer's approval of the workflow run can let the unit tests start, and no action here can supply it.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - allow 10 more repair and 10 more sync attempts and continue, though the run stops again until a maintainer approves the workflow run.
3. assess - stop the delivery work and post nothing, since no problems are open.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case D: own PR with a ready repair

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR is meant to make the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. That behavior is not covered yet, because the endpoint still reports a fixed version, and nothing in the PR is deferred or handled elsewhere.

One problem blocks merging: the health endpoint returns a hardcoded version string instead of the build version, so every deployment reports the same version whatever was built (src/health.ts:8). The test health_version in tests/health.test.mjs fails on this. A repair is drafted that reads the existing build-version value.

I recommend deliver because the drafted repair fixes your own PR and you can push it.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review comment and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case E: another author's PR with a description-only problem

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR by robin makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are a requested reviewer. The ticket's requirement that the health endpoint report the build version is covered, and the README describes that behavior correctly.

One problem blocks merging: the description says the endpoint "Reports uptime", but it returns only the build version (src/health.ts:8). A reader of the description would expect uptime data that never arrives.
Proposed correction: "Reports uptime" -> "Reports the build version"

I recommend deliver because the drafted description correction resolves the only problem and needs no decision from the author.

Pick one:
1. deliver - apply the drafted description correction, merge main into the branch if it falls behind, watch the checks, and continue until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review requesting changes and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case F: another author's PR, and you cannot push

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR by robin is meant to make the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are a requested reviewer. That behavior is not covered yet, because the response lacks the version field, and nothing in the PR is deferred or handled elsewhere.

One problem blocks merging: the health endpoint's response has no version field, so callers cannot learn which build is running (src/health.ts:8). The test health_version in tests/health.test.mjs fails on this. Repairing it here is not offered because you cannot push to this branch.

I recommend assess because posting this problem gives robin the concrete fix to make.

Pick one:
1. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review requesting changes and make no repairs. [recommended]
2. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case G: pending contract proposal

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

Current wording: the build version is served at /health.
Proposed wording: the build version is served at /status.

Today the spec requires the build version to come from the existing health check address. Moving it to the new status address gains nothing toward serving the build version and changes the address callers must use. I recommend preserve contract because the existing health check can return the same build version without changing the spec.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep the spec's requirement and resume the repair so the existing health check returns the build version. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - amend the spec to require the new address, then resume delivery.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

The proposal moves that response to a different endpoint, but the existing health handler can deliver the goal without changing the requirement. Pick one:

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: The Case G rewrite is what moved facts: After shows a Current/Proposed wording pair that keeps /health and /status, then gives exactly three path-free sentences above Pick one (current requirement, what moving the address costs or gains, why the existing health check can already return the build version), and its rows carry no paths or extra argument. That flips contract to holds, and it also flips authority, because Before's G had only a one-sentence proposal summary plus a recommendation reason containing both paths rather than the three contract sentences. No fact that Before kept was lost, but two After wordings are close to the edge and worth tightening. In Case A the deliver row now says 'one more 15-minute window and continue until merge is offered', which a strict reader could take as open-ended watching rather than exactly one additional window; Before's 'for one more 15-minute window, without adding repair or sync attempts' is safer. Also in Case A, the parenthetical '(test_unit)' puts a raw check identifier in the report prose; keep it as 'the unit tests' to stay clear of the internal-names rule. In Case B, 'retry the merge check' is acceptable only because it is conditioned on 'once another reviewer has approved'; keep that condition at the start of the row so it never reads as a retry promised now.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: The only fact that moved is contract, and it moved because After's Case G shows a separate Current/Proposed wording pair carrying /health and /status, then explains the pick in three sentences that contain no path, ID or field name; Before put /health inside the explanation and showed no wording pair. Before's two paragraphs of proposal prose are gone, and preserve contract stays recommended at row 1 with accept contract change and stop after it. The pass is narrow on one point: the second sentence says the proposal "moves that response to a different endpoint" but states the cost or gain only by implication, so the wording should require that sentence to say concretely what the change costs or gains (for example, that callers of the existing address would lose the response and nothing is gained because the goal is already reachable). The third sentence should stay dedicated to why the existing address can already serve the build version. Cases A-F kept every fact; to keep them, hold the reason sentence directly above Pick one, keep stop last and non-recommended where it is not the pick, keep Case B's deliver row opening with the another-reviewer condition, and keep the exact "Reports uptime" to "Reports the build version" preview in Case E. Two small risks to watch: the "add 10 repair attempts and 10 sync attempts" phrasing in B and C sits close to the banned repair/sync counters, and Case C's stop reason is now stronger than Before's because it names the unchanged approval blocking every continuation, which is worth keeping.
